hints.title: Unsorted Interval Overlap Obstacle
hints.text: Intervals can arrive unsorted with arbitrary overlaps. Comparing all pairs to check for overlap takes quadratic time. How can sorting intervals by their start points ensure that overlapping intervals are always adjacent in the sequence?

hints.title: Adjacent Boundary Overlap Invariant
hints.text: When intervals are sorted by start time, a subsequent interval overlaps with the prior merged interval if and only if its start time is less than or equal to the prior interval's end time.

hints.title: Sort and Linear Merge Procedure
hints.text: Return the intervals if empty. Sort intervals in ascending order by their start times. Initialize a result list with the first interval. For each subsequent interval, check if its start time is less than or equal to the last merged interval's end time; if so, update the end time to the maximum of both. Otherwise, append the interval as a new disjoint entry.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(N log N) time; merging takes a single O(N) linear pass.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing and merging all pairs iteratively takes O(N^2) time and requires complex repeatedly updated graph components.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting by start coordinates guarantees adjacent overlaps, taking O(N) space for sorted output.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct interval sorting key, in-place expansion of merged interval end time, handling nested and touching intervals.
